targets.authors: Rogenmoser L, Elmer S, Jäncke L
targets.title: Absolute pitch: evidence for early cognitive facilitation during passive listening as revealed by reduced P3a amplitudes.
targets.evidence_quote: In the present study, we attempted to replicate Rogenmoser et al. (2015)’s finding of electrophysiological group differences between AP and non-AP musicians during passive listening.
targets.outcome_quote: In summary, our direct replication of Rogenmoser et al. (2015) successfully replicated the non-significant results for group differences in the MMN. In contrast, we did not replicate the finding of smaller P3a amplitudes in AP musicians.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly state that the MMN null finding replicated and contrast this with the failed P3a finding. These are both focal comparisons within the one original paper; general implications for the cognitive account do not erase the stated agreement and disagreement.

reasoning: Article title and all four authors match. New larger musician sample directly re-tests one original paper. Other earlier EEG papers are discussed as background rather than additional replication targets.
